score.label: Score
score.derived: the babble's weighted total, sum(score x weight) / 5

rows.name: Shell
rows.thesis: The site is a terminal session: clickable commands whose output is the UI, with real pictures inside the output.
rows.best_when: The visitor is a developer who wants to find a part, see it, check its sources and copy the code.
rows.loses_when: Browsing visually or a non-technical visitor — outputs pile up as history and the prompt bar costs ~80 px.

rows.name: Drawing Sheet
rows.thesis: Every part is an engineering drawing sheet — dimensioned views, a spec list, a title block and a provenance block.
rows.best_when: Judging size and envelope, and where each number came from.
rows.loses_when: Browsing for looks — the register shows drawn thumbnails, and specs scroll inside the sheet on desktop.

rows.name: Catalog
rows.thesis: McMaster-density catalog: category tree and dense rows lead to a long part page with a photo column, spec table and offers.
rows.best_when: You already know roughly what you want and need to scan, filter and compare many parts quickly.
rows.loses_when: You want the feel of a developer tool or a terminal; this reads as a store catalog.

rows.name: Views
rows.thesis: An Ultra Librarian-style multi-panel viewer: one panel per layer of the black box, side by side, toggleable and maximisable.
rows.best_when: You want the whole part — pictures, specs, offers and code — on one screen.
rows.loses_when: Browsing many parts — the explorer list is plain and it is the least narrative variant.

rows.name: Notebook
rows.thesis: Each page is an executable reference notebook: real code cells and their outputs — figures, tables and plots.
rows.best_when: The visitor is a developer who wants to read and copy the code that gets the data.
rows.loses_when: Someone wants to look at a part fast — code chrome costs vertical space, and on a phone the picture is below the first screen.

rows.name: McMaster
rows.thesis: McMaster-Carr's catalog logic: category index with spec buckets, dense family tables with a picture on every row, and a part page with photo + always-visible drawing + buy box.
rows.best_when: You know roughly what you want and scan many parts fast in dense tables.
rows.loses_when: The visitor wants something visual or curated; the landing's three dense columns can read as a wall of links.

rows.name: PCPartPicker
rows.thesis: PCPartPicker's shopping logic: picture-led browse, filterable tables with compare, and a part page centred on prices across sellers, price history, region and the level as the 'rating'.
rows.best_when: Shopping or shortlisting — filter, compare two or three, and see who sells each at what price, checked when.
rows.loses_when: Pictures should carry the part page; views sit in one-at-a-time tabs and price chrome overweights thin shipping data.

rows.name: Views + Offers
rows.thesis: Ultra Librarian's part page (four views side by side, each with its own selector and download) plus Octopart's distributor offer table, behind a search-first home.
rows.best_when: You want each part's first screen to be four labelled pictures of it, then who sells it — a distributor + component-model site.
rows.loses_when: You want one dominant hero picture or McMaster density; for PSUs and cameras one of the four panels is an honest empty slot.

rows.name: Parametric
rows.thesis: DigiKey/Mouser parametric search: every spec is a filter with a histogram and live counts, a full-width results table, and a part page led by the attributes table and 'similar parts'.
rows.best_when: You know the spec ('3–6 N·m, under 0.2 kg, in stock') and want to narrow 1,146 actuators and compare in columns.
rows.loses_when: Someone is just looking — filter boxes and tables lead, pictures follow.

rows.name: Gallery
rows.thesis: Adafruit/SparkFun/Misumi product browsing: a picture-card grid with views badges and facets, and a top-down part page with a big views carousel, key-spec tiles and a buy box.
rows.best_when: A human lands and browses by picture — scan photos and drawn envelopes with price and stock, peek, then open a part.
rows.loses_when: Density matters — about 8 parts per screen against ~15 rows in a table, and it reads most like a store.
